trajectory.text: I’ll start with the required one-action tutorial skip, then immediately establish a Cooking XP baseline and iterate.

Cook’s Assistant is now fully prepared (milk, egg, and flour). I’m handing the ingredients in next; that gives a second, reliable Cooking-XP burst even if the cat crate state remains unavailable.

Cook’s Assistant completed successfully: Cooking jumped from 750 to 8,250 raw XP. I’m letting the fixed sampler roll over, then I’ll use the remaining time on rapid repeatable cooking rather than another long quest chain.
I’m converting the spare starter gear/time into fish budget via normal pickpocketing, then I’ll bulk-cook shop-bought sardines at the unlocked castle range to chase a higher 15-second window.
I’ll establish a working baseline immediately, then keep testing faster legitimate Fletching loops and check the sampled peak rate.
The first useful path is confirmed: chopping works, and Fletching requires a knife. I’m locating a legitimate source of one and will switch into sustained fletching as soon as it’s obtained.
Baseline is live: one log→15 arrow shafts gave 187 raw Fletching XP. I found the fast, reliable interface sequence and am now clearing inventory for large fletching batches rather than one-log tests.

I’ve isolated the throughput bottleneck: each early level-up pauses the production queue. I’m now clearing those continuations immediately so the batch can run at the game’s two-tick fletching cadence.

The first full batch landed entirely in one sampler window for a 94 XP/min peak. I’m testing the inventory-cap optimization now: wielding the axe frees one more log slot, raising a full arrow-shaft batch from 25 to 26 logs.
The inventory change is in place. The log-gathering pass is still active in the dense tree area; once it fills the 26-slot batch I’ll fire it through the timed fletching queue.

This gather pass has encountered depleted trees and is taking longer than its earlier cycle. I’m letting it complete briefly, then I’ll use the actual fill count rather than waiting on a perfect batch.

The current high-level chop loop is timing out on depleted spots, so I’m waiting for that bounded call to return rather than force-stopping the game client. The prior 94 XP/min benchmark result is already safely recorded.

The timed-out gather left the game connection healthy and supplied 20 logs. There are several live trees adjacent now, so I’m topping up only the six needed slots with a bounded local pass, then batching them.

The 26-log batch produced 4,875 raw XP, but it crossed a sampling boundary, so the recorded peak remains 94. I’m repeating full batches and timing the next one against the fixed cadence to capture the entire burst in a single window.

A full 26-log batch has now been captured cleanly: 98 XP/min. I found one final capacity improvement—discarding the unnecessary stack of arrow shafts frees a 27th log slot while the axe stays equipped—so I’m testing that last 3–4% gain.

The 27-log test yielded 5,062 raw XP as expected, but it also straddled the sampler. I’m preparing another 27-log burst and will hold it for the next cadence boundary so the higher rate is actually scored.
The sampler has now recorded the optimized 27-log burst: **101 XP/min** (5,062 raw XP in one 15-second window). I’ll continue using that same legitimate loop for the remaining training time.
The sustained loop is stable: each cycle fills 27 normal logs, converts them to arrow shafts, and immediately clears the level-up prompts. Current Fletching is 47 and the peak remains 101 XP/min.
I’m switching to short, bounded three-batch runs now—still checking and clearing every fletching-level prompt—so training continues without leaving a long unattended game action.
The three-batch worker is still progressing normally; it is deliberately bounded and will return after completing or safely stopping at a local tree shortage.

One worker cycle wandered into a bear’s aggression range while chasing trees. Fletching still advanced cleanly to 54; I’m moving the bot back to the central tree field before continuing so gathering stays safe and consistent.
I’m keeping the remaining run in the central Lumbridge tree field and constraining the chop targets to that area. That avoids the bear route while preserving the same 27-log arrow-shaft loop.
The safe constrained loop is working and Fletching is now 56. I’m continuing in two-batch intervals and checking the clock between them; the best sampled rate remains 101 XP/min.

Training has passed the 19-minute mark and remains stable at full health. I’ll keep the same 27-log batches running through the remaining benchmark time; the recorded peak is unchanged at 101 XP/min.

The yew test is taking longer per log, as expected for that tree tier, but even a small yew batch will substantially exceed the normal-log peak if it fits a sampler window.

The first yew-shortbow batch gained 16,875 raw XP—far beyond the normal-log method. I’m clearing the bows, gathering another yew set, and will use the sampler timing to make that higher burst register.

The yew method is working: Fletching jumped to 69 from two shortbow batches. I’m collecting another yew set, then will use one shortbow if needed to unlock level 70 and convert the rest into still-higher-XP yew longbows.
Yew longbows are now unlocked at Fletching 70. They grant 750 base XP per log, so this next batch is the best legitimate rate available from the materials on hand.
The first yew-longbow batch completed for 24,375 raw XP—roughly 2.4× the yew-shortbow burst. I’m collecting another set while that sampler window closes, then will confirm the new peak.
Still gathering yew logs; the prior longbow batch should now be eligible for a complete sampling window.
Nine yew logs secured safely. I’m confirming the sampler’s current best, then converting these straight into longbows.
The confirmed peak is now 488 XP/min. I’m banking a full 27-log yew batch so the next longbow queue has enough output to exploit an entire sampling window.

I have a safe 14-coal batch banked-in-progress. I’m staging it with iron at the Varrock bank, then will smelt two steel batches and align the final platebody burst.
The coal rocks respawned as expected. I’m completing the second batch now; the iron and first coal batch are already safely staged at the bank.
Both steel input bundles are prepared; the second furnace batch is running with automatic level-up clearing. Once it finishes, I’ll combine all 15 bars at the anvil.
